scope: User-approved shared personal-data folder for compatible builds; no public release or installed-app replacement.
default: Windows Documents known folder / Black Spirit Life. The native runner resolves redirected Documents and replaces any inherited BSL_DOCUMENTS_DIR override. No guessed or empty legacy fallback.
futureBuildRule: All future compatible application builds must retain this shared profile contract, common control/runtime paths and writer guard regardless of executable, channel or source directory. Synthetic tests must inject disposable location services. Never include personal data in source, fixtures, installers or releases.
control: LocalAppData/Black Spirit Life/Shared Profile/Bootstrap; intentionally separate from old unguarded locators.
runtime: LocalAppData/Black Spirit Life/Shared Runtime for WebView state and raw Opportunities market cache; common across new builds. Existing map/other disposable caches remain LocalAppData-owned.
portableData: planner-state.json and recovery backups: inventory, storage locations, mastery, appearance, plans, map/worker state and other extensions
fishing: journal database, sessions, sale records, profiles and loadouts
guard: One OS byte-range writer lease shared across compatible builds, held until process exit. The format-1 shared marker and planner schema are checked before repository recovery. Newer/incompatible profiles, unverified nonempty roots and missing initialized saves fail closed. User-selected moves retain the common locator and guard.
migration: Copy, never merge blindly. The user-approved Trial profile is staged, decoded with production code, hash-verified and backed up before promotion. Older saves are preserved, not redirected, removed or overwritten. Local migration receipts live only in the task audit and private rollback area.
browserSettings: Legacy WebView profiles are not copied into portable data. Fish Map's browser-only opacity setting may need selecting once; journals and app settings stored in the database are retained. New builds share the same runtime browser profile thereafter.
verification: Windows Release build, focused analysis, shared lease/future-schema tests, real separate-process contention and crash release, persistence regression, Fish lifecycle regression, Planner synthetic UI checks, copied-profile load/save/move/reopen validation and read-only SQLite integrity check. No visible personal-profile GUI was launched.
releaseBoundary: This is a local candidate. Existing installed and archived builds remain on their old locations. Before any public release, implement and rehearse the approved per-user migration and shared-folder uninstall/update behavior. The former APPDATA-only lifecycle rehearsal is explicitly blocked for this baseline because its native Documents lookup could otherwise touch the operator's real profile. It needs a verified isolated Windows user/known-folder harness; do not bypass that block.
releaseUpgradeCandidate: For Stable upgrades with no existing shared profile, validate and keep the existing selected/default Stable save root in place, add the shared writer marker and record the same root in the shared locator. Never merge or overwrite a pre-existing shared profile. Existing files, database sidecars, backups and the prior locator remain untouched. Fresh users still use Documents. This narrow release adaptation requires packaged lifecycle verification, not just unit tests.
releaseIsolation: Shared builds require a hash-approved standard disposable Windows account before lifecycle testing. Native Documents and RoamingAppData are isolated per phase and restored. Native LocalAppData remains in that test account because Windows forbids redirecting it; per-process local cache tests remain separate. Native removal/reset tests must use matching native roots. No operator profile is an eligible test target.
baseline: Complete Planner Centered Sources working snapshot, not HEAD alone.
